sources.entry: Checklist of the most important security countermeasures when designing, testing, and releasing your API

summary.one_liner: A checklist of API security countermeasures covering authentication, authorization, input and output handling, CI/CD, and monitoring.
summary.what_it_does: This is a Markdown checklist, not software, of security measures to apply when designing, testing, and releasing an API. It is organized into sections: Authentication, Access, Authorization (with OAuth items), Input, Processing, Output, CI & CD, and Monitoring. Each item is a checkbox with a short directive, such as avoiding Basic Auth, using HTTPS with TLS 1.2+ and HSTS, validating redirect_uri, sending nosniff and frame-deny headers, and using UUIDs instead of auto-incremented IDs. The README also has an appended "Advanced" section covering rate limiting, GraphQL hardening, secrets management, and zero-trust practices. A short "See also" section points to a related API development resource list and suggests random API keys instead of JWT in some cases.
use_cases: checking an API design before release
reviewing API security during code review
building a pre-launch security checklist for REST APIs
hardening API response headers and error messages
planning CI/CD security gates for an API
notable: Covers the full API lifecycle, from design and authentication through CI/CD and monitoring
Gives concrete header values such as X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'
Includes OAuth-specific items such as rejecting response_type=token and using state for CSRF protection
Translated into more than 25 languages in the README header
Includes an advanced section on GraphQL, secrets management, and zero trust
caveats: Items are brief directives without implementation detail or code examples
The advanced section is appended with items that differ in style and depth from the original checklist
Not a tool; it does not scan or enforce anything
